videos.script: A Go program that works on your machine still has to reach somebody else's. This lesson ships hits, and makes sure the copy that arrives is the one you built. {{static}} It starts with the binary. Go can build one that needs nothing from the system: no C library, no loader. You will see when that happens by itself, and when it takes CGO_ENABLED=0. {{image}} Then a container image, built in two stages. The first holds the Go toolchain and compiles hits. The second, called distroless, holds the binary and almost nothing else. Nine hundred megabytes of workshop become an image under six. It runs as a user who is not root, and there is no shell inside. {{scratch}} Next, the image with nothing in it at all, called scratch. A small program asks it three questions, and all three fail. Distroless answers them from a handful of files, and you will count them. {{sign}} Last, trust. A checksum shows that the bytes did not change. A build anybody can repeat shows where they came from. And a signature, made with cosign, shows who stands behind them. You will forge a file and watch the check refuse it.
